close_reason: PKITS oracle disproves this finding. NIST PKITS §4.6.8/4.6.14 explicitly place CA certs (cA=TRUE) at chain[0] and require MUST-VALIDATE. RFC 5280 §6.1 path validation does not require chain[0] to be an EE cert — that is an application-layer check (EKU/purpose). The i>0 guard is correct behavior per the normative test suite.
description: chain[0] is never checked for BasicConstraints cA=TRUE or cA=FALSE. A CA certificate placed at chain[0] (the leaf position) passes all BasicConstraints and KeyUsage checks because the i>0 guard skips all CA-only checks for the leaf. An attacker or misconfigured caller can pass a CA cert as the end-entity and the path validator accepts it. RFC 5280 §3.3 and common path-validator practice require the EE to not be a CA cert.
title: leaf cert with cA=TRUE not rejected
